relationship.statement: A simple pendulum's swing period increases with the square root of length and decreases with gravity, while mass has no effect because force and inertia both scale with mass.
assumptions: Release angle stays fixed at 25 deg in the small-angle regime.
Air resistance and pivot friction are neglected.
The rod is massless and rigid; the bob acts as a point mass.

quantities.label: Rod length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the test pivot to the center of the pendulum bob

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the test pendulum bob, affecting both weight and inertia

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration pulling the test pendulum downward

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Initial angle from vertical, held at 25 deg for small-angle motion

quantities.label: Reference length
quantities.meaning: Length of the reference pendulum, fixed at 1.0 m

quantities.label: Reference gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravity for the reference pendulum, fixed at 9.8 m/s^2 on Earth

quantities.label: Test period
quantities.meaning: Time for one complete back-and-forth swing of the test pendulum

quantities.label: Reference period
quantities.meaning: Time for one complete back-and-forth swing of the reference pendulum

quantities.label: Test weight
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational force on the test bob (mass times gravity)

quantities.label: Peak restoring accel
quantities.meaning: Maximum tangential acceleration along the arc at the turning points

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var g = inputs.gravity; var refL = 1.0; var refM = 1.0; var refG = 9.8; var theta0Deg = 25; var theta0Rad = theta0Deg * Math.PI / 180; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var refOmega = Math.sqrt(refG / refL); var testPeriod = 2 * Math.PI / omega; var refPeriod = 2 * Math.PI / refOmega; var testTheta = theta0Rad * Math.cos(omega * t); var refTheta = theta0Rad * Math.cos(refOmega * t); var testAngle = testTheta * 180 / Math.PI; var refAngle = refTheta * 180 / Math.PI; var testX = 1.0 + L * Math.sin(testTheta); var testY = -L * Math.cos(testTheta); var refX = -1.0 + refL * Math.sin(refTheta); var refY = -refL * Math.cos(refTheta); var testWeight = m * g; var refWeight = refM * refG; var testPeakAccel = g * Math.sin(theta0Rad); var arrowScale = 0.025; var testForceTipY = testY - arrowScale * testWeight; var refForceTipY = refY - arrowScale * refWeight; var testPlumbY = -L - 0.12; var testBobSize = 0.15 + 0.3 * m; var refBobSize = 0.15 + 0.3 * refM; var diffPeriod = testPeriod - refPeriod; var sameLg = Math.abs(L - refL) < 0.05 && Math.abs(g - refG) < 0.05; var isMassOnlyDiff = sameLg && Math.abs(m - refM) > 0.05; var isFaster = diffPeriod < -0.02; var isSlower = diffPeriod > 0.02; var isBalancedMatch = Math.abs(diffPeriod) < 0.02 && (Math.abs(L - refL) > 0.05 || Math.abs(g - refG) > 0.05); return { testPeriod: testPeriod, refPeriod: refPeriod, testWeight: testWeight, refWeight: refWeight, testPeakAccel: testPeakAccel, testAngle: testAngle, refAngle: refAngle, testX: testX, testY: testY, refX: refX, refY: refY, testForceTipY: testForceTipY, refForceTipY: refForceTipY, testPlumbY: testPlumbY, testBobSize: testBobSize, refBobSize: refBobSize, isMassOnlyDiff: isMassOnlyDiff, isFaster: isFaster, isSlower: isSlower, isBalancedMatch: isBalancedMatch }; }

lesson.title: What Changes a Pendulum's Swing?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum to a fixed Earth reference (1 m, 1 kg) as you vary length, mass, and gravity. Watch the diagram and angle plot reveal what actually changes the swing period.
lesson.instructions: Adjust Rod length, Bob mass, and Gravity one at a time while keeping the others at defaults (1.0 m, 1.0 kg, 9.8 m/s^2). Compare the test wave against the reference wave and check the weight force and peak acceleration readouts.
lesson.goal: See that pendulum period depends only on length and gravity, not mass, because extra mass increases weight and inertia equally.
